- read this before using any number.** This artifact was produced on **Sun 2026-11-01 08:47 ET**, about **46 hours after the scheduled fire**, because the original 2026-10-30 09:00 ET run died on the platform's Token Plan quota wall (error 2067) and this session is the resumed instance of that same fire (`cron_read view=runs` → run_id 457983592751486, `scheduled_at_ms` = 2026-10-30 09:00:00 ET).

**TL;DR**

- **The single biggest mover of the day was a $300M REIT that a naive screen cannot see.** ARI
- gapped **-63.9%** pre-market: Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance, which disclosed on Oct 16 that it was **liquidating and expected to end its NYSE listing**.
- It is sub-scale by every conventional filter, but it is a $300M market cap with a real pre-market print and a real reason to trade.

- **Intel was the trigger for the rest of the tape.** INTC gapped **-25.7%** on a Q4 guide
- ($15.0–16.0B revenue vs ~$17.07B expected; adj. EPS $0.25 vs $0.43) that broke the beat-and-raise pattern the whole AI-infrastructure trade was priced on.
- The read-through ran through the physical supply chain — DELL -12.4%, HPQ -15.1%, AMD -10.1%, and the semi-equipment complex (UCTT -10.4%, AEHR -10.5%, ONTO -9.3%) repriced together.

- **Two idiosyncratic blowups dwarfed the macro move.** ATEC gapped **-39.8%** on a Q3 revenue
miss plus a 2026 revenue-guidance cut to $862M, and RDDT gapped **-22.8%** on weaker-than- expected DAU and a Q4 revenue guide below consensus — its worst one-day decline ever.

- **A second, quieter wave ran through the REITs and mortgage lenders.** ABR (Arbor Realty)
- gapped **-16.2%** on a Q3 loss, a **dividend suspension** and a $53M loan-loss provision; BBUC gapped -23.3% on a 100-share print.
- That is a credit story, not the AI story, and it is invisible in the first edition of this brief.

- **The bid went to defensives.** Consumer staples +1.4%, energy +1.9%, health care +0.7%, with
Coca-Cola, Walmart, Eli Lilly and Berkshire all up over 1% — a rotation out of AI beta, not a flight out of equities.

**Top gappers — reconstructed pre-market prints**

- Gap % is TradingView's `premarket_change` for 2026-10-30, measured against the **official Oct-29 regular-session close** (shibui).
- "PM vol" is cumulative pre-market shares with that volume as a % of the 30-day average daily volume (`average_volume_30d_calc`) — the honest importance measure.
- "PM range" is the pre-market low–high from Yahoo's archived tape, **shown only where Yahoo's tape agrees with TradingView within 0.6%**;
- "n/a" means Yahoo's tape was stale for that name and no range is published. Mkt cap is $M. All gaps are ≥3% on ≥$200M market cap.

- **481 further names** at ≥3% pre-market gap (55 gainers, 468 decliners in total) are carried in the `_raw/tv_oct30_auth.json` row set, and 235 more beyond the published table sit at ≥5%.
- Names with no confirmed catalyst carry that mark rather than an inferred cause.

**Catalysts — the deep dives**

Per the skill's cap, deep dives are limited to **five** names; every other row above carries a one-line attribution from the same morning's coverage.

- **ARI (-63.9%) — a liquidation, and the day's largest move.** Apollo Commercial Real Estate
- Finance disclosed on Oct 16 that it was **winding down and expected to end its NYSE listing**, and an Oct 30 Schedule 13G/A from Vanguard recorded a 219,335-share position.
- At $2.33 the stock was down 76.7% over twelve months and 62.4% over the month.
- The pre-market volume was 67,528 shares — **1.6% of a normal day's volume** — so the gap is a real print on a thin book, not a liquid repricing.
- This name is invisible to any screen that filters to common stock, which is why it was missing from the first edition of this brief.

- **ATEC (-39.8%) — a guidance cut on top of a miss, in a name already under investigation.**
- Q3 revenue of $221.2M (+12.6% y/y) missed the $225.2M consensus and adjusted EPS of $0.09 came in below the $0.10–0.11 range;
- management attributed the outlook reduction partly to a **slump in add-on bone-graft product sales**, with fewer surgeons buying matting used in spinal-fusion procedures.
- The **2026 revenue guide was cut to $862M from ~$882M consensus**. BMO downgraded to Market Perform with an $8 target; Wells Fargo cut to $12 while keeping Overweight.
- Against that, Levi & Korsinsky and Ademi LLP both announced securities-fraud investigations on Oct 30. It closed at $7.04, **-38.08%**, near its 52-week low of $6.81.

- **RDDT (-22.8%) — the DAU and the guide, not the revenue.** Revenue of $895M (+53% y/y) beat the
- $878M consensus and EPS of $1.40 beat $1.35. But **daily active uniques came in at 130M against 133.7M expected** ,
- with the US down 2% to 50.7M against 53.5M expected, and CEO Steve Huffman disclosed that **search referral traffic dropped by over 1 million per week on average in October**.
- Q4 revenue was guided to **$1.00–1.03B against a $1.05B consensus**. Reddit's plan to move to a **logged-in-only experience** — trialing internationally this quarter —
- is read by JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth as a sound attempt to reduce Google search reliance that "will likely take time." Downgrades followed:
- Oppenheimer to Perform, KeyBanc to Sector Weight, Evercore ISI and Citizens downgrades, Bernstein's target the worst at $120.
- It closed **-29.22%**, its worst one-day drop ever, below $100 for the first time since May 2025.

- **ABR (-16.2%) — a dividend suspension and a $53M provision, in the mortgage-credit complex.**
- Arbor Realty Trust reported a **GAAP net loss of $85.4M** ($0.51/share) against net income of $38.5M a year earlier, a **distributable loss of $0.04** against $0.35, and a **$53.0M CECL loan-loss provision** with non-performing loans rising to 32 from 19.
- The board **suspended the quarterly common dividend** to preserve capital. Revenue of $94.1M missed the $112.7M consensus and net interest income of $37.7M missed $48.6M by 22.5%.
- It closed **-29.14%** — its worst day ever, down 81.5% over twelve months. That is the credit half of Friday's tape, and it had nothing to do with AI.

- **CDNA (+14.7%) and GDYN (+10.3%) — the two clean beats that were not AI-spending stories.**
- CareDx reported adjusted EPS of **$0.70 against $0.25 expected** and revenue of **$139.4M against $120.6M** ,
- then **raised FY26 revenue guidance to $520–530M from $490–500M** (consensus $489.7M) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90–100M against $68.5M expected, with an AlloHeme launch planned for Q1 2027.
- Grid Dynamics posted **EPS of $0.18 against $0.1252** and revenue of $114.29M against $112.77M — above the *high end* of its own guidance —
- with record non-GAAP EBITDA of $22.9M (20% of revenue) against a $16.5–17.5M guide, **AI revenue +45% y/y and now ~32% of total**, and revenue per employee above $100,000 for the first time.
- Both are AI *beneficiaries* rather than AI *spenders*, which is the distinction the day turned on.

---

**Themes**

- **The market repriced the return on AI capex, not the demand for it.** Alphabet's search-advertising miss on Oct 29 (stock -12.6%, its worst day on record, roughly $500B of market value) and Amazon's earnings the same night with trailing-12-month free cash flow at **-$42.4B** formed one argument:
- the industry is spending faster than it can show returns. The Nasdaq Composite fell **2.86%** (worst day since June 5), the SOX **7.2%**, and the Nasdaq-100 erased over $1T.
- Intel's 17 price-target cuts turned a single-name disappointment into a sector event.

- **The transmission ran through the physical supply chain, not the software layer.** The names that gapped hardest were not AI applications —
- they were the companies that physically build the datacenter:
- server makers (DELL -12.4%, HPQ -15.1%), semi-equipment (UCTT -10.4%, AEHR -10.5%, ONTO -9.3%), connectivity (MXL -9.3%, AAOI -9.3%) and power (BE -8.9%).
- Software that *sells* into the AI build-out (GDYN +10.3%, RMNI +20.3%, ASUR +21.3%) gapped **up**.

- **Two credit stories ran underneath the AI story.** ABR's dividend suspension and BBUC's collapse were mortgage-REIT events with their own causes, and both sat inside a market-wide risk-off tape where they were easy to mis-file as AI read-through.
- **A screen that excludes REITs cannot see them at all** — which is exactly how the first edition of this brief lost ARI, the day's largest mover, and ABR.

- **Guidance, once again, was the dividing line — and it cut in both directions.** INTC, TWLO, ILMN and RDDT all beat the quarter and were sold.
- OSPN, CDNA, GDYN, RMNI and ASUR beat and were bought.
- TWLO is the cleanest example: it beat Q3 *and* raised full-year guidance, and still fell 23.5% pre-market because Q4 organic growth was guided to 11–12% from 16%.

---

**Needs human eyes**

- **ARI's gap is real but thin, and the stock is going out of business.** 67,528 pre-market shares
is 1.6% of a normal day, and the underlying story is a liquidation ending the listing. Anyone reading -63.9% as a tradeable dislocation is reading a delisting, not a mispricing.

- **ABR is a balance-sheet story, not an earnings story.** A dividend suspension plus a $53M
- provision plus non-performing loans rising from 19 to 32 is a credit event.
- If the mortgage-REIT complex keeps breaking down, it is a separate theme from AI and it deserves its own screen.

- **Intel's Israel fab and the memory shortage are two shocks, and only one is temporary.** The
- Fab 28 explosion is a one-off (~$300M of Q4 revenue); the memory-driven PC contraction is forecast through H1 2027.
- Intel Foundry grew 58% and still lost $1.85B — the turnaround's core is the part of the business the market is not paying for.

- **ATEC carries an active investigation on top of a guidance cut.** Two firms announced
securities-fraud investigations on Oct 30. Those notices do not establish wrongdoing, but they change the risk profile of a stock already at its 52-week low with a cut guide.

- **Pre-market volume separates the real moves from the quotes, and it is now in the table.** 283 of
- the 523 names traded under 1% of a normal day's volume pre-market. BBUC's -23.3% moved 100 shares; HRTG's -11.5% moved 2,000; NPB's +11.3% moved 177.
- Against that, INTC moved 21.6M shares (18.9% of ADV) and RDDT 1.5M (26.7%). **The % of ADV column is the single most important column in this brief.**

- **A gap can fade before the open.** The pre-market print is a snapshot; several names sat at the
edge of their range. Nothing here is a 09:30 open instruction.

**Method & caveats**

- **This is a reconstruction, not a live capture.** The original 09:00 ET run died on the Token Plan
- quota wall (error 2067) — the delivery auditor's `audit/status` branch records this session (457983151079669) with status 2 and the 2067 message, and no `ntrt/2026-10-30.md` existed on any ref.
- This resumed instance rebuilt the brief from the **TradingView public screener**, whose `premarket_*` columns still hold the 2026-10-30 session because the market has not reopened since.

- **This edition corrects two defects in the first edition, and the corrections are material.**
- The first edition seeded its universe from shibui filtered on `type = 'Common Stock'`, which **excluded REITs** and dropped 178 names including **ARI (-63.9%)**, the day's largest mover.
- It also read prices from Yahoo's archived bars, which **carry no pre-market volume** and go **stale** for thinly-traded names —
- 13 of the first edition's top 40 had a stale Yahoo tape, and ADT's stale print ($7.46) understated a stock that opened +33%.
- TradingView screens `type = stock`, which includes REITs, and supplies volume for all 523 names.

- **Independent validation.** The published Oct-30 pre-market table (StockAnalysis, retrieved
- 2026-11-01) agrees to the cent on every overlapping name:
- ARI -63.88% at $2.33, ABOS -85.15% at $0.34 (below the $200M floor and therefore excluded here), ATEC -39.8%, INTC -25.7%, RDDT -22.8%, BBUC -23.26% at $22.01, TWLO -20.9%, ABR -18.5%, OABI -17.2%.
- `market-recap.get_quotes` confirms the settled Oct-30 closes with an `as_of` stamp of 2026-10-30T20:00:01Z, and shibui's official Oct-29 closes are the gap denominator.

- **TradingView's pre-market snapshot is one moment, not the last trade.** On fast names it
- differs from the published table by 1–4pp (NPKI: TV -27.7% vs published -23.7%); the published table confirms TV on the overlapping names.
- The Yahoo pre-market range is published **only where it agrees with TV within 0.6%**, so a stale range can never appear next to a correct price.

- **Relative volume is a 30-day daily proxy.** `average_volume_30d_calc` is a trailing 30-session
average, not an intraday measure; the "% of ADV" column is PM volume against that average, which is the honest importance measure and the same construction the 2026-10-28 brief used.

- **The `ntrt_mtrt` backend and the MCP finance tools are both absent.** `GET
- http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` refuses connection and no `NTRT_BASE_URL` is set, so skill Mode A was unavailable; `mcp__tradingview_advanced__*` and `mcp__yahoo_finance__*` are not registered in this runtime (confirmed again 2026-11-01:
- catalog 133 tools, 0 finance), so the skill's Mode B screener was reached through its **public HTTPS endpoint** rather than the MCP tool.
- This repo's own `ntrt/_pipeline/fetch_screen.py` already does exactly that, and it is the source this edition uses.

- **Catalyst coverage is deliberately uneven and marked as such.** Five names carry researched
- catalysts; the rest carry a one-line attribution or an explicit "no confirmed catalyst" mark. Where no cause was identified, no cause is inferred.
- Deep dives are capped at five per the skill spec.

- **Index levels for the session are from the reconstructed tape, not this brief.** SPY -1.77%
($755.72), QQQ -3.47% ($690.49), Nasdaq Composite -2.86% (25,437.00), from `market-recap` and press.
